candidates.name: Thermal noisy labels of the input point (Z = Y + theta, theta ~ K_A = e^{F(A)-A}, A a ferromagnetic cosine form, updated adaptively)
candidates.statement: Attach to the input point Y a label Z = Y + theta mod 1 whose error law has density K_A proportional to exp(-sum_s lambda_s(1 - cos 2 pi s y)). Spectra and transforms are read through the label: G^u = int |E[a chi_u(Y) K_A(z-Y)]|^2 / E[a K_A(z-Y)] dz measures how much the label reveals the phase chi_u(Y). Each successful spectral update adds a spatial form S_p and a metric form D_i to A, so the noise concentrates (in the error variable) on a smooth Bohr set of the discovered frequencies. Integrating a label character recovers the scalar transform at a shifted frequency multiplied by c_A(n), which is close to 1 for representatives.

neighbours.ref: Bourgain, 'On triples in arithmetic progression', GAFA 9 (1999); Sanders, Annals 2011 / Bogolyubov-Ruzsa (arXiv:1011.0107); Bloom-Sisask exposition of Kelley-Meka (arXiv:2302.07211)
neighbours.relation: K_A is a smoothed (Gibbs-weighted) Bohr set in the error variable: theta concentrates where ||s theta|| is small for every heavily weighted s. Conditioning on Z = Y + theta therefore localises Y to a random translate of a Bohr set, which is the density-increment step of Bohr-set arguments. In those arguments one restricts to a translate and gains density; here one keeps the whole input, carries the label as side information and pays for it in Fisher information.
neighbours.verdict: related principle (randomised Bohr-set localisation); genuinely different mechanism and use

family_D.correctness_caveat: All grades are conditional on correctness. The claim is extraordinary: it resolves the L log L conjecture and gives a new proof of Carleson's theorem. It is unrefereed. The Lean (156 files, ~29.2k lines, sorry/axiom-free at text level, Mathlib-only, exact comparator match) was not built here. It formalises a different parametrisation and only the eps_j = r_{j+1} case of Prop dyadic, and it never states the paper's simultaneous regular-evidence proposition.
family_D.compression_note: No step-3b inlining measurement is available for 075. The label (frac 0.26) is the only new object above the 20% proxy, and as a definition it is small and pervasive, the profile of an extension variable. Whether inlining it causes multiplicative blow-up is untested.

provenance_flag.explanation: All 23 references are human literature. The only 2025-2026 citation (Di Plinio-Fragkos 2025) is a 2022 arXiv preprint with no AI disclosure and none of the candidate items. Web searches for the problem with 'ChatGPT', 'GPT-5', 'OpenAI' and 'AI-assisted' returned only the October 2026 release coverage (which does not single out this family) and human papers. OpenAI's August 2026 'Ten Advances' collection does not treat this problem. The paper itself is model-produced (author 'OpenAI', dated 2026-09-23). Caveat: the release is three days old, so later disclosures could not be checked.

bridge_novelty.import: Information theory -> Carleson-type maximal estimates (entropy chain rules, Fisher information, noisy channel)
bridge_novelty.status: new bridge for this problem type
bridge_novelty.evidence: No information-theoretic proof of any Carleson-type bound found (searches on information-theoretic / entropy / mutual-information proofs of Carleson; Lacey's survey math/0307008 and Demeter's guide 1210.0886 list only time-frequency proofs). 'Entropy' in the Fourier-series literature means level-set or metric entropy (Fefferman 1978; Bourgain's entropy method), not Shannon entropy. The general route 'entropy -> large spectrum' is known (IMR 2014; Lee 2017), but not for pointwise convergence.

bridge_novelty.import: Additive combinatorics (Chang's lemma, dissociated spectra, Riesz products, Bohr-type balls) -> Carleson operator
bridge_novelty.evidence: Lie's papers (arXiv:1902.03630 appendix; Polynomial Carleson, Annals 2020) explicitly connect additive combinatorics with time-frequency analysis and expect structural additive-combinatorial theorems to matter. Chang/Bohr-set machinery used as here (to compress a separated spectrum) was not found.

Petermichl's shift and Hytonen's averaging are standard. Maximally modulated Haar multipliers are known Carleson models (arXiv:1506.00861 App. A).

P-C1.hide: I26, I24 (thermal forms), I27 (Fisher sum), I29-I31, I33-I36, I38-I42 and all of Secs 5-9. Keep I12 (compression) only in arm A.
P-C1.arm_A_pivot: Give Prop dyadic (I32) as the target, plus I12 compression, I10 (two laws U vs P) and the observation 'information under P is bounded by d'. Directed sentence: 'Find an auxiliary random object that lets you pay for selecting frequencies with information about the input point.' A high hit rate is plausible here.
P-C1.arm_B_cluster_decisive: Give only Prop dyadic as the target, the reduction I05/I32 and L. No compression, no two-law framing.
P-C1.equivalence: Hit if the proposal (a) attaches to the input point Y a random observation Z = Y + noise (or an equivalent Markov kernel), whose noise law is adapted to frequencies already found so that it is nearly invariant under them (a smooth Bohr-set or Gibbs-type law), and (b) reads modulated coefficients through Z and charges the resulting information to an entropy budget O(d). (a) without (b) is partial credit. Deterministic Bohr-set restriction (density increment) without a noisy observation is a near-miss, recorded separately. Lean target: OAI.FourierLLogL.Thermal.channel.

P-C3.arm_A: Directed: give the separated-spectrum setting of I28 (a set S of frequencies with uniform noisy-sum moment bounds) and ask for a structural lemma usable for every later weight.
P-C3.arm_B: Open: give Chang + Lee only and ask for the strongest structure theorem under the moment hypothesis (05:349-367).
P-C3.equivalence: Hit if the statement yields a large subset S' (log-loss o(k_b)) and a single centre with a common weighted phase region valid uniformly for all weights on S'. A Chang-type 'spectrum in a low-rank Bohr set' without uniformity in the weight is partial credit. Lean target: Compress.entropy_compression.

P-C4.hide: I22 and its proof; keep I21 (gluing) and the obstruction paragraph removed.
P-C4.equivalence: Hit if the proposal reaches the block-length target with O(D^2/(E h^2)) one-letter entropy loss, through a schedule that handles non-shrinking widths p_j (two orders, or an equivalent amortisation). A single-order telescoping with a worse loss is a miss.

P-C5.hide: I29 and the gap assertions of I30.
P-C5.equivalence: Hit if the proposal is a monovariant comparing the free energy (log-measure) of the smooth spatial Bohr set e^{-A} with the log-size of its nearly-annihilated frequency ball, which drops on cheap updates. Any potential that closes the k_b/count budget counts as partial credit. Lean target: Thermal.gap.

P-C7.hide: I32 and Secs 3-9; give I05 and Petermichl-Hytonen.
P-C7.equivalence: Hit if the proposal is an L1 bound Cd for a maximally modulated Petermichl-type shift with stopping at a polylog(d) density cutoff.
